info.name: SyncBeat WebSocket (STOMP) - Frame Reference
info.description:
Frame-text REFERENCE for the mainframe's STOMP-over-WebSocket layer (see syncbeat-service-breakdown.md — Backend API Service — WebSocket layer). Pairs with SyncBeat-Mainframe.postman_collection.json for {{room_id}}/{{track_id}}.

**Important: Postman does not support importing/exporting native WebSocket requests as collection JSON** (confirmed open limitation — see postmanlabs/postman-app-support issues #11252 and #12316). The items below are plain HTTP-shaped placeholders that will NOT behave as real WebSocket requests if you hit Send on them — they exist purely so the exact STOMP frame text for each step is versioned, readable, and copy-pasteable from inside Postman's sidebar.

**Actual workflow (all manual, in Postman's native WebSocket UI):**
1. Run the REST collection's Auth > Register, then Auth > Login, then Rooms > Create Room (sets {{room_id}}, makes that user the room's host — only the host can send playback actions).
2. Run '0. Login (capture access_token)' below to populate {{access_token}} from the httpOnly cookie (see its description for the manual fallback if pm.cookies.get comes up empty).
3. New > WebSocket Request in Postman. URL: ws://localhost:8080/ws. Click Connect — expect HTTP 101, not 401 (if you get 401, the mainframe needs SecurityConfig's /ws/** permitAll fix + a restart — see PROGRESS.md).
4. In the Message pane, paste each frame below IN ORDER and hit Send after each one, on this SAME connection: 1. Connect's body first, then 2. Subscribe, then whichever of 3-6 you want to test, then optionally 7. Unsubscribe and 8. Disconnect. Postman resolves {{access_token}}/{{room_id}}/{{track_id}} inside the message text against your active environment same as any other request.
5. Authorization header on the CONNECT frame is the raw JWT — no 'Bearer ' prefix (WebSocketSecurityConfig's STOMP channel interceptor reads the native Authorization header verbatim, unlike the REST filter which strips that prefix).
6. Cmd/Ctrl+S on the native WS request lets you save the URL into a collection for reuse — the frame sequence itself still has to be pasted per session since STOMP is a live, ordered, stateful exchange, not a request/response pair.
7. To see the broadcast loop close, open a second native WebSocket connection subscribed to the same room topic — actions sent by the host should echo back to both once syncbeat-sync's consumer is actually running and relaying through Redis Pub/Sub.

request.description: Same endpoint as the REST collection's Auth > Login — duplicated here only so this collection is self-contained. Requires the account to already exist (run the REST collection's Auth > Register first, or edit the email/password below to an existing user). Sets {{access_token}} from the httpOnly access_token cookie via the test script; that user becomes the room host if they're also the one who ran Rooms > Create Room.

exec: console.warn('access_token cookie not found — open Cookies under Send, copy access_token manually into the {{access_token}} environment variable. This can happen if Postman enforced the cookie\'s Secure flag over plain http.');

item.name: STOMP frames (send in this order, over ONE open connection)

request.description: First frame on the connection. Authorization is the raw JWT from {{access_token}} — no 'Bearer ' prefix. Expect a CONNECTED frame back; anything else (or a closed socket) means the token was rejected.

Send this on the SAME connection opened in step 1. Ties this socket to room {{room_id}} — server-side, this is what triggers RoomChannelSubscriptionManager to start listening to the room's Redis Pub/Sub channel (once per room per instance, not per subscriber).

Only accepted if {{access_token}}'s user is the room's host (checked against Redis room state) — otherwise PlaybackController logs a warning server-side and silently drops it (no error frame yet, see PROGRESS.md known deferred items). On success this publishes a PlaybackEvent to SNS; you won't see anything come back over THIS socket until syncbeat-sync consumes it and the mainframe rebroadcasts to /topic/room/{{room_id}}.
Needs {{track_id}} — run the REST collection's Tracks > Create Track first (or paste any existing track id).

id must match the SUBSCRIBE frame's id (sub-0). Server-side this drops the local ref-count in RoomChannelSubscriptionManager; once it hits zero for this room on this instance, the Redis Pub/Sub listener for room:{{room_id}} is torn down.

Graceful close. Also try just closing the socket without sending this — that exercises RoomSubscriptionEventListener's SessionDisconnectEvent path (unsubscribe + RedisService.removeMember), which is the other thing this collection exists to test.
